rules.P1: The shares add up: approve + disapprove + no opinion is 100 within 1.5 points (or approve + disapprove is at most 100 when no opinion isn't given).
rules.P2: The dates are in order: fieldwork starts before it ends, and ends before the results were published.
rules.P3: The margin of error isn't smaller than the sample allows: at the stated confidence level, simple random sampling gives a floor; a survey can claim more than that (design effects), never less.
rules.P4: Every poll names its source: the pollster's report or a news report, with a link.
rules.P5: No poll is entered twice: one row per pollster and publication date.

text.eyebrow: Opinion polls · 9 polls, April 2025 to July 2026
text.lede: The latest polls disagree: Global InfoAnalytics put President Mahama's job approval at 72% in July 2026, the IEA at 58.9% in May 2026. TARIN lists every published national poll on the president's performance it can trace, with who ran it, when, how many people were asked and where each figure was read.
text.tile-1-l: approve · Institute of Economic Affairs, May 2026
text.tile-2-l: national polls from 2 pollsters since April 2025
text.tile-3-l: apart: the IEA and Global InfoAnalytics, polling within 20 days of each other
text.c-p: Each point is one poll, placed at the middle of its fieldwork. Where the dates weren't published it sits at the date the results came out, drawn hollow. Lines join polls by the same pollster; nothing is averaged.
text.d-p: In December 2025 Global InfoAnalytics and the IEA were 1 point apart (67% and 68%). In May–June 2026 they were 12.1 points apart: the IEA found 58.9% (May 2026), Global InfoAnalytics 71% (30 May – 12 Jun 2026).
text.m-src: Where the figures come from. 2 of the 9 polls are read from the pollster's own report; for the other 7, the pollster's report wasn't found online, so the figures come from news reports of the release, linked in the table. A figure the source doesn't give is left blank, never filled in.
